summary: @whalent/agent-core ships a fully obfuscated remote-shell agent with PTY + WebSocket control channel
details: The package's main bundle dist/index.cjs (~13.7 MB) is wrapped in a rotating obfuscator.io string-array decoder (a0_0x187d) with no plaintext URLs, headers, or command strings anywhere in the file. Runtime dependencies include ssh2 and the optional dependency node-pty, and the obfuscated bytes reference WebSocket, Authorization, process.env.SHELL, and loopback ports 127.0.0.1:3389 and 127.0.0.1:5900/5901 (RDP/VNC). This composition wires a network transport (WebSocket, authenticated) to a local PTY/shell on the host running the agent: an inbound remote peer can drive interactive shell sessions and reach local RDP/VNC endpoints. The README further states this package "is replaced by remote daemon upgrades," i.e. the running agent accepts server-side instructions to swap its own code — an unbounded remote code-load channel with no visible pinning or signature verification. All exfiltration/C2 destinations are hidden by the obfuscation, so the network peer that ultimately controls the shell is not identifiable from source.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
